summary: The root دَهَنَ (dhn) primarily means to anoint or oil something, like hair or skin. It can also describe rain lightly moistening the earth.
lane: 1 دَهَنَهُ دهن دهنه دهننه دهنة , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. دَهُنَ , (S, Msb,) inf. n. دَهْنٌ (MA, Msb, K, KL) and دَهْنَةٌ , (K,) He anointed it (MA, Mgh, Msb, * KL) with دُهْن , (Mgh, Msb,) i. e., (Msb,) with oil (MA, Msb, KL) &c.; (Msb;) [ oiled it; or greased it; ] namely, his head, (MA, Mgh,) or his mustache, (Mgh,) or his hair, &c.: (Msb:) or he moistened it; namely, his head, &c.: (K:) and , inf. n. تَدْهِينٌ signifies the same [but app. in an intensive sense, or as applying to many objects]: (TA:) and إِدْهَانٌ [inf. n. of ] is like تَدْهِينٌ . (AHeyth, TA.) -b2- [Hence,] دَهَنَ الأَرْضَ , said of rain, (S, K,) (tropical:) It moistened the ground slightly, or a little: (S, TA:) or it moistened the surface of the ground. (K.) -b3- And [hence also,] دَهَنْتُهُ بِالعَصَا (S, K *) (tropical:) I struck him (S, K, TA) gently (TA) with the staff, or stick; (S, K, TA;) like as one says, مَسَحَهُ بِالعَصَا and بِالسَّيْفِ . (TA.) And دَهَنْتُهُ بِالعَصَا دَهَنَاتٍ (tropical:) I struck him [ gently ] with the staff or stick [ some gentle strokes: دَهَنَاتٌ being pl. of , which is the inf. n. of un.]. (So in a copy of the S.) -b4- [Hence, likewise,] دَهَنَ signifies also He (a man, TA) played the hypocrite. (K, TA.) And you say, دَهَنَ فُلَانًا , aor. دَهُنَ , inf. n. دَهْنٌ , meaning He acted with such a one hypocritically. (TK. [See also 3.]) -A2- دَهُنَتْ , (K, and so in more than three copies of the S,) and دَهَنَتْ , aor. دَهُنَ ; (K, and so in some copies of the S in lieu of دَهُنَتْ ;) and دَهِنَتْ , aor. دَهَنَ ; (AZ, K;) inf. n. [of the first] دَهَانَةٌ (S, K) and [of the second or third or of both] دِهَانٌ ; (K;) (tropical:) She (a camel) had little milk. (AZ, S, K, TA.) [See دَهِينٌ .] -b2- And دَهِنَ , inf. n. دَهْنٌ , [or, as appears to be probable from what follows and from general analogy, دَهَنٌ ,] said of a man, (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, weak: and also, foolish, or stupid: and [app. soft, flaccid, or flabby; for] دَهَنٌ signifies the being soft, flaccid, or flabby; or softness, flaccidity, or flabbiness. (JK.) [See دَهِينٌ .]

headwords.def: دَهَنَهُ دهن دهنه دهننه دهنة, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. دَهُنَ, (S, Msb,) inf. n. دَهْنٌ (MA, Msb, K, KL) and دَهْنَةٌ, (K,) He anointed it (MA, Mgh, Msb, * KL) with دُهْن, (Mgh, Msb,) i. e., (Msb,) with oil (MA, Msb, KL) &c.; (Msb;) [ oiled it; or greased it; ] namely, his head, (MA, Mgh,) or his mustache, (Mgh,) or his hair, &c.: (Msb:) or he moistened it; namely, his head, &c.: (K:) and, inf. n. تَدْهِينٌ signifies the same [but app.
دَهَّنَ see 1, first sentence.

مُدَاهَنَهٌ مداهن مداهنه مداهنة and signify the same; (S, Msb, K;) i. e. (tropical:) The endeavouring to conciliate; syn. مُصَانَعَةٌ: (S, TA:) or the making peace with another; or becoming reconciled with another: (Msb:) or the pretending the contrary of, or what is different from, that which one conceals in his mind: (K:) and the former signifies also the acting with dishonesty, or dissimulation: or ↓ the latter has this signification; and the former signifies the striving to outwit, deceive,…

ادهن أد أدهن إد إدهن ادهن دهن ودى آد آدهن, inf. n. إِدْهَانٌ: see 1, first sentence: and see 3, in six places. [See also its act. part. n., below.] الإِدْهَانُ is also syn. with الإِبْقَآءُ, which, accord. to IAmb, is the primary signification: in the copies of the K erroneously written الإِنْقَآءُ. (TA.) One says, لَا تُدْهِنْ عَلَيْهِ, meaning لَا تُبْقِ عَلَيْهِ [ Show not thou mercy to him; or pity not him; or pardon not him ]. (IAmb, TA.) And مَا أَدْهَنْتَ إِلَّا عَلَى نَفْسِكَ, i. e.
تَدَهَّنَ see what next follows.
اِدَّهَنَ أد أدهن إد إدهن ادهن دهن ودى آد آدهن, of the measure اِفْتَعَلَ, He anointed himself with دُهْن, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) i. e. oil, &c.; (Msb;) [ oiled, or greased, himself; ] as also. (S.)
Q. Q. 2 تَيَدْهَنَ تيدهن He (a man) took a مُدْهُن [q. v.]. (S.)
دَهْنٌ دهن دهنن: see دُهْنٌ. عَيْشٌ دَهْنٌ Bad and scanty [ means of subsistence ]. (JK.)

دُهْنٌ دهن دهنن Oil, (MA, Msb, KL,) &c., (Msb,) [i. e. grease of any kind, ] or دُهْن [i. e. oil ] of sesame &c., (Mgh,) with which one anoints, (Mgh, Msb,) [or greases, ] or moistens, (K,) the head or mustache, (Mgh,) or the hair &c., (Msb,) or the head &c.: (K:) it is well known: (S:) and signifies a portion thereof: (K:) [or this latter, being the n.

دِهْنٌ دهن دهنن A kind of tree with which beasts of prey are killed, (JK, K,) and by means of which they are taken: (JK:) it is a noxious tree, like the دِفْلَى [q. v.]: (TA:) n. un. with ة. (K.) And Such as is large, of trees. (JK.)
دَهِنٌ دهن دهنن Oily, or greasy. (KL.) You say also رَجُلٌ meaning دَهِنُ الشَّعَرِ [ A man having oily, or greasy, hair ]. (TA.) [See also دَهِينٌ.]
دَهْنَةٌ دهن دهنه دهننه دهنة; pl. دَهَنَاتٌ: see 1.

دُهْنَةٌ دهن دهنه دهننه دهنة: see دُهْنٌ. Also Odour: so in the saying هُوَ طَيِّبُ الدُّهْنَةِ [ He, or it, is sweet in respect of odour ]. (K. [Erroneously written and explained by Golius in his Lexicon.])

دَهْنَآءُ دهنآء A [ desert such as is termed ] فَلَاة: (K:) or a place of sands: (JK:) or a place all sand: (TA:) [or a desert of reddish sand. Hence,] with the article ال, A certain place [or desert tract ] belonging to Temeem, in Nejd, (S K, TA,) extending to the distance of three days' journey, in which is no water; (TA;) as also الدَّهْنَى; (S, K;) this latter occurring in poetry. (TA.) [The same appellation is also applied to The great desert of which the central part lies towards the S.
[ دُهْنِيَّةٌ دهني دهنيه دهنية An oily quality. ]

دِهَانٌ دهان دهن A red hide. (S, K. [See also دَهِينٌ.]) Hence, in the Kur [lv. 37], فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ, i. e. And shall become red, (S,) or of a rosecolour, (Zj, L in art. ورد,) or of a red colour inclining to yellow, (L in that art.,) like the red hide: (S, Bd, Jel:) or like the hide that is of a pure red colour: (TA:) or like that [ oil ] with which one anoints; see دُهْنٌ: or it is pl. of دُهْنٌ: (Bd:) [thus] it means, accord.

دَهِينٌ دهى دهي دهين [ Anointed with oil, &c.; i. q. and مَدْهُونَةٌ ]. You say لِحْيَةٌ دَهِينٌ (K) and دَهِينَةٌ (TA) and, (K,) [the last, properly, a possessive epithet,] meaning مَدْهُونَةٌ [i. e. A beard anointed with oil, &c. ]. (K, TA.) And A hide intensely red. (JK. [See also دِهَانٌ.]) Also, applied to a she-camel, (JK, S, K,) (tropical:) Having little milk: (S, K:) or having very little milk; (JK;) not yielding a drop of milk (JK, TA) when her dug is squeezed: (JK:) accord.
دَهَّانٌ دهان دهن A seller of oil: (MA, TA:) and a maker of oil. (MA.) [In the present day, it is applied to A painter of houses &c. ]
دَاهِنٌ داهن داهنن: see دَهِينٌ.
مُدْهَنٌ مد مدهن A camel affected with the vertigo termed دُهْن. (JK.)

مُدْهُنٌ مد مدهن, with damm, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) only, (S,) to the م and ه, (Msb, TA,) extr [in form], (Fr, TA,) for by rule it should be مِدْهَنٌ, (Msb,) or it was مِدْهَنٌ originally, (Lth, TA,) The utensil ( آلَة ) for دُهْن [or oil, &c. ]; (K, TA;) i. e. (TA) the thing [or pot or vase ] in which دُهْن is put; (T, Msb, TA;) a flask, or phial, ( قَارُورَة,) for دُهْن: (S, K:) [and, occurring in this art. and in art. وقب in the TA, signifies the same:] pl. مَدَاهِنُ.

مُدْهِنٌ مد مدهن [act. part. n. of 4, q. v.]. أَفَبِهٰ َا الحَدِيثِ أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ, in the Kur [lvi. 80], means Do ye then reject this announcement? or disbelieve &c.? (TA:) or hold in light, or little, or mean, estimation, (Bd, Jel,) and reject, &c.? (Jel.)
مَدْهَنَةٌ مدهن مدهنه مدهنة A place where oil is made; an oil-mill. (MA.)
مُدْهُنَةٌ مدهن مدهنه مدهنة: see مُدْهُنٌ.
قَوْمٌ مُدَهَّنُونَ قوم مدهنون (tropical:) A people, or company of men, upon whom are [ visible ] the traces of ease and plenty, welfare, or well-being. (S, K, TA.)
مَدْهُونٌ مدهون: see دَهِينٌ. [Hence,] أَرْضٌ مَدْهُوَنَةٌ (tropical:) Land moistened slightly, or a little, by rain. (S, TA:) or having its surface moistened by rain. (TA.)
مُدْهَانٌّ مدهان: see دَهِنٌ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
